findings.rationale: Migration output is planned from bytes read earlier, but commit checks only that the pathname currently names a regular file before renaming over it. No lock, digest comparison, or inode precondition ties the write to the reviewed source, so an editor save or concurrent migration between planning and rename is silently discarded; competing processes can both report success.

The document-check command accepts approval records but no trust keys, and its V2 branch converts a signed record directly to its binding while propagating the claimed key ID without verifying the signature. A forged or modified signed approval can therefore be incorporated into the expected rendering and a correspondingly forged stakeholder document can be reported conformant.

The evaluation compares current specification, artifact, generator, claim-set, and reviewed-artifact digests, but the command returns nonzero only when status is exactly signature-invalid. Other non-current evaluation statuses therefore produce exit code 0, allowing an exit-code-based CI approval gate to accept a drifted approval.
